body:
P2-25 DESIGN, part 3: the stored keys, the repair, and how a split reaches the phones (docs/tasks/P2-songs-as-references.md, parts 7 to 9).

WHAT A WRONG ATTACHMENT IS IN THE DATA: not a ref_merge row (a tombstone means two refs shared a FILE: real evidence) but ONE live ref holding several song_file rows of different music-server songs (find matched the second Arabic file to the first Arabic ref by the key, attach_file obeyed). link_library then keeps the file there on every pass (the holder rule), so prevention alone repairs nothing.

STEP 1, at start-up, before any thread and BEFORE refmerge.repair (keyrepair.py; precedent refmerge): when setting.textnorm_revision is below TEXTNORM_REVISION (first value 1; the old fold is 0): backup before-key-rewrite, then ONE transaction: every song_ref.norm_key is rewritten; a rewrite NEVER merges (two refs that share a new key stay two); the worklist is filled; the revision is written last; idempotent, rolls back whole, logs, never stops the server. The suspect test is on the ref own text (does its lead artist or title survive the OLD fold: era 0 of survives_fold_whole, frozen as _lost_by_old_fold), NOT on the stored key (fairuz|habibi| is not empty). Worklist = new table ref_recheck(ref, at, moved), no foreign key (like file_log.ref and ref_gone.ref_id), only suspect refs that hold at least one library-source song_file; the keeper files (source youtube or quality) are never re-judged. Tombstones: ref_merge.norm_key cannot be recomputed (no title or artist stored): a key with an empty segment is set to NULL (it can never be found again; ids still resolve), the others stay (dead weight, never a wrong answer); NEW nullable columns ref_merge.title and artist, filled from now on, so the next revision can rewrite tombstones (decision D10).

STEP 2, in the hourly library link (rehome.py), not at start-up: song_file.meta holds no title or artist, the scan reads the tags anyway, and a start-up that waits for the music server does not start. For EVERY library row of a worklist ref (not only the scan holder, which is the oldest row only), judged by the tags of the song the pass reads: refs.find on the tags (ids first, then the new key, then tombstones): if it returns this ref, KEEP; otherwise MOVE the row (UPDATE song_file SET ref, nothing else changes: id, added_at, meta, source kept; a target that already holds the same song keeps one row; one preferred file per ref; touch_file and touch_ref_holders on both). No usable tags: not judged. A COMPLETE pass deletes the worklist rows it read. One backup before the first move. rehome.py re-points song_file rows and NOTHING else: it must never rename, move, retag or delete a file of the Host's own music library (a stranger's music folder); only a keeper file under Encore/ may be moved, by the refile of N-34, never by the rehome; a test row says a library file is only ever re-pointed. refmerge now HOLDS a pair when either ref is on the worklist (reason recheck_pending): merging identities on the strength of a file that may be on the wrong ref would put one song likes on another.

THE PHONE (read): files_since returns the CURRENT state of every ref with a file_log row after the cursor, with the whole description; a moved file is two rows (old ref, new ref); upsertRefs inserts the new one and updates the old; the old ref audioKey changes so its download is stale by the key it already has (download_planner.dart:116-118). So: no new feed, no tombstone, no ref_merge, no ref_gone; every like, entry, play, queue position and download stays on the old ref, which keeps the first title. WEIGHED: (A) move files (chosen); (B) re-create ids or reverse merges: rejected (ref_merge.old_id is UNIQUE and merges_after reads by seq at read time, so deleting a tombstone makes two phones disagree; RefMerger on the phone already moved downloads, likes and entries); (C) never split: rejected (the album that says 1 song stays so for ever).
